jurisdiction.name: Papua New Guinea
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Papua New Guinea has no adopted AI instrument yet. Its AI governance is a 2026 package of consultation drafts from the Department of Information and Communications Technology: a government AI adoption framework that sets red lines such as no AI-only decisions on people's rights and no citizen scoring; a National Sovereign AI and Digital Transformation Strategy proposing a National AI Act and new AI institutions; and a Data Governance and Data Protection Bill with interim risk-based AI rules, including human review of automated decisions and prohibited AI practices.
lead_institutions: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the ICT department's website and consultation portal. There is no searchable online National Gazette, and whether the data protection bill has been introduced in Parliament remains to be confirmed. The proposed National AI Act and announced deepfake laws are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Draft released for public consultation: the Acting Minister for ICT's press statement of 22 March 2026 says the Draft Strategy would be published on 23 March 2026 at www.ict.gov.pg. As of 13 October 2026 DICT still lists it under 'Draft Policies' (feedback to feedback@ict.gov.pg) and says stakeholder consultations are under way; no adoption or NEC endorsement has been found.
instruments.summary: Draft national strategy built on the model 'Digital Government x Digital Public Infrastructure ^ AI', adopting a layered National Sovereign AI TechStack (governance, connectivity/compute/cloud/data, DPI such as SevisPass/SevisPay/SevisDEx, shared government services, workflows, business intelligence) as the reference model for reform and investment. Its governance framework proposes a Prime Minister-chaired Ministerial Committee on Digital Transformation and AI, a Digital Transformation and AI Board, a restructured Department of Digital Transformation and AI and an independent National Digital Economy Authority, with an approval/assurance lifecycle, human oversight for high-impact uses and rules for AI public agents. It also proposes a National Artificial Intelligence Act (risk-based, technology-neutral), a Data Governance and Protection Act, a Digital Identity and Trust Framework Act and a Critical Digital Infrastructure Investment Act.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: PNG's first national AI strategy (consultation draft); sets the proposed institutional and legislative architecture for AI governance.

Listed as a draft on DICT's Draft Policies page. Not yet verified from the official text: Part 2 (Government Implementation Pack: governance, standards, safeguards, rollout plans binding on agencies), which the draft references.
instruments.summary: Plain-language Part 1 of the draft whole-of-government AI adoption framework, explaining the 'Digital Government x Digital Public Infrastructure ^ AI' logic and a five-layer modular architecture in which AI sits on top of shared national infrastructure and DPI. It sets red lines for government AI use: no AI-only decisions on rights, benefits or penalties, no secret citizen scoring, no use of data outside lawful purposes, no untested AI in high-impact services, protection of cultural heritage, and no uncontrolled external AI systems in core decision-making. It also describes citizens' protections (privacy, human review, appeal and complaint pathways) and defers detailed agency rules to Part 2.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Draft public-sector AI adoption and safeguards framework for all PNG public bodies.

instruments.english_title: Data Governance and Data Protection Bill 2026 (fifth draft for public consultation)
instruments.issuing_authority: Department of Information and Communications Technology (with NICTA), Government of Papua New Guinea
instruments.current_status: Government draft Bill under public consultation from 6 August to 21 August 2026; the Minister for ICT's statement of 6 August 2026 says he instructed DICT and NICTA to expedite it for introduction in the September 2026 sitting of Parliament, but no evidence of introduction or passage has been found. The current text is the undated 'Proposed Draft – 5th Version' (the date recorded is the consultation opening date), and commencement would be by notice in the National Gazette (s. 2), with Parts IV-XIII able to commence on different days. Consultation closed on 21 August 2026.
instruments.summary: Draft Bill giving legal effect to the National Data Governance and Data Protection Policy 2024, covering personal and government data, data-subject rights, breach notification, cross-border transfers and sovereign hosting, with NICTA deemed the National Data Authority on an interim basis. It contains an interim risk-based AI framework: public bodies may not make decisions affecting rights or access to significant public services solely by automated means without meaningful human review (s. 69), individuals get a right to human review of AI/automated decisions with Tok Pisin notices (s. 70), and Part VIII sets responsible-AI principles, high-risk system duties (DPIA, bias testing, audit records, transparency, registration with the Authority), prohibited practices (subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, government social scoring, real-time remote biometric identification without court authorisation, election/judicial manipulation) punishable by fines up to K5 million, and chatbot disclosure duties. Part VIII applies until a dedicated national AI law is enacted.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First draft legislation in PNG with binding-style AI rules (interim AI governance pending a National AI Act).

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Papua New Guinea's ICT department legislation and consultation pages, the Prime Minister's department, ministries and regulators were searched. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for binding law, procurement, cybersecurity, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sectoral rules, generative AI, international agreements or historical publications. It remains to check Parliament's bills page, whether the data governance bill has gone to Parliament, whether the AI strategy consultation has closed, and the AI content of a scanned 2024 data policy.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. parliament.gov.pg bills page 404; no online searchable gazette. Strategy (i-5c2920c03033) re-identified as consultation draft dated 2026-03-23 per Acting Minister's statement of 22 Mar 2026 (PDF undated); o-8e671932a90a renamed in place; s-b3d74ab827c1 kept. Adoption Framework Part 1 dated 2026-02-27 from cover. DGDP Bill 5th draft dated 2026-08-06 (consultation opening; PDF undated); recorded as government consultation draft (introduction in Parliament not confirmed). National Data Governance & Data Protection Policy 2024 scanned, no OCR (lead). Digital Government Act 2022, Digital Transformation Policy 2020, Cloud Policy 2023 AI in passing. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: No enacted AI law or AI provisions found. Searched: ict.gov.pg Legislations (Digital Government Act 2022 - no AI provisions, NICT Act 2009), ICT Legislation Consultation (Data Governance and Data Protection Bill 2026 - recorded as consultation draft; Cybersecurity Bill 2026 notice - no AI provisions; Verifiable Credentials Bill). parliament.gov.pg bills page returned 404; PacLII used only for discovery, nothing found. Deepfake/Cybercrime Code amendments announced only (lead).; Government: DICT: draft Government AI Adoption Framework Part 1 (recorded), draft National Sovereign AI and Digital Transformation Strategy (recorded), Part 2 Implementation Pack not online (lead). Endorsed policies checked for AI content: Digital Transformation Policy 2020 and Government Cloud Policy 2023 mention AI only in passing; National Cyber Security Strategy 2024-2030 and Social Media Policy 2025: no AI content; Data Governance & Data Protection Policy 2024 scanned (lead). Dept of PM & NEC (pmnec.gov.pg): only news on AI intentions, no documents.; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no AI documents from education, health, justice, defence, treasury/finance, labour or interior ministries surfaced in searches of gov.pg sites.; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: no standalone data protection authority exists (NICTA proposed as interim National Data Authority in the DGDP Bill); NICTA, Bank of PNG and National Cyber Security Centre - no AI-specific documents found.. Not reached: parliament.gov.pg bills register (page returned 404; no AI bill found via search); National Gazette (Government Printing Office) - no online searchable gazette reached. Could not verify: National Data Governance & Data Protection Policy 2024 (scanned PDF; no OCR available) - AI content and date unverified.; Whether the DGDP Bill 2026 was introduced in Parliament in September 2026 (parliament.gov.pg bills page 404).; Whether consultation on the AI Strategy / Adoption Framework has closed or any final version was endorsed by NEC.. binding-law, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, international, historical: no material found.
